summary: Direct x86_64 machine instructions, hardware CPU registers, stack pointers, and system call execution.

rows.means: copies data between CPU registers or between memory and registers
rows.consequence: x86_64 cannot move directly from memory to memory in a single instruction; data must load into a register first.

rows.code:
ADD dst, src
SUB dst, src   -- sets ZF CF SF OF
rows.means: performs arithmetic addition and subtraction on registers
rows.consequence: Arithmetic also writes the condition flags — zero, carry, sign and overflow — which is how the next instruction knows what happened without being told.

rows.means: compares two operands by computing (op1 - op2) without saving result
rows.consequence: Sets CPU flags based on the subtraction result, immediately followed by conditional jump instructions.

rows.code: JMP label   -- writes the instruction pointer
rows.means: unconditional jump: replaces the instruction pointer with the target address
rows.consequence: A direct jump: the address of the next instruction is replaced, which is what every loop, branch and function return is made of underneath.

rows.code:
JE / JZ   (jump if equal / zero)
JNE / JNZ (jump if not equal / not zero)
rows.means: jump if the previous comparison was equal, or if it was not
rows.consequence: Conditional branches read the flag the previous arithmetic set, which is why a comparison and the branch that uses it must not be separated by anything that also writes flags.

rows.code:
CALL label
RET   -- pushes and pops the return address
rows.means: calls subroutine / returns to caller address
rows.consequence: CALL puts the address of the following instruction on the stack and jumps; RET takes it off and jumps back. The call stack is not a language feature here, it is these two instructions and a register.

rows.code:
PUSH src
POP dst   -- adjusts RSP
rows.means: pushes value onto stack (decrements RSP) / pops into register (increments RSP)
rows.consequence: The stack grows downward, from high addresses towards low ones, so pushing subtracts from the stack pointer and the deepest frame has the lowest address.

rows.means: 64-bit / 32-bit accumulator register; stores function return values
rows.consequence: By calling convention, functions return their numeric or pointer result in RAX.

rows.code:
RSP (stack pointer)
PUSH / POP / CALL / RET adjust it
sub rsp, 32   -- allocate a frame by hand
rows.means: points to the top of the current thread execution stack
rows.consequence: Moved automatically by the stack instructions, or by hand to make room for locals — which is what a function prologue is, once the language is taken away.

rows.means: frame pointer pointing to the base of current stack frame
rows.consequence: Historically used to index function local variables and arguments; modern compilers often omit it (-fomit-frame-pointer).

rows.code: RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9   -- first six integer arguments
rows.means: the registers this platform's calling convention uses for arguments
rows.consequence: The calling convention used on these systems passes the first six integer or pointer arguments in registers rather than on the stack, which is why a function with few arguments never touches memory to receive them.

rows.code: RIP (instruction pointer)   -- not writable by MOV
rows.means: register holding the memory address of the next instruction to execute
rows.consequence: Cannot be assigned directly; it is changed by jumps, calls and returns. That restriction is the reason control flow is a small fixed set of instructions rather than arithmetic on an address.

rows.code:
LEA dst, [src + offset]
lea rax, [rdi + rsi*4 + 8]
rows.means: loads an effective address: computes an address without touching memory
rows.consequence: Computes an address without reading memory, which is why it gets used as a fast multiply-and-add: the address arithmetic unit does the work the arithmetic instructions would have.

rows.code: SYSCALL   -- number in RAX, arguments in RDI, RSI, RDX
rows.means: hands control to the kernel, leaving the program's own privilege level
rows.consequence: Hands control to the kernel with the call number in a register and the arguments in the argument registers. Everything a program cannot do for itself — open a file, write output, exit — goes through this one instruction.

rows.means: does nothing, and occupies space while doing it
rows.consequence: Does nothing, and is used to pad so that a loop target begins on an address the processor fetches efficiently. An instruction whose only purpose is where the next one starts.
